titleEn: Sumerian King List — Utuhegal, Ur, and Isin (VIII 3 – VIII 46)
about: The end of the prism: Col. VIII 3–46. After the Gutians the kingship returns to Uruk, where Utuhegal is its one king, for a reign the prism writes as '7 years, šu-ši, 7 days' — Langdon's '7 1/6 years and 7 days', a reading that is not certain. Uruk is smitten and the kingship goes to Ur, where Ur-Namma, Shulgi, Amar-Suen, Shu-Suen and Ibi-Suen reign; the prism counts them as 4 kings and 108 years, though it names five and their reigns add up to 106. Then Ur is smitten and the kingship goes to Isin: fourteen kings, from Ishbi-Erra to Suen-magir, whose reigns, with three figures restored by Langdon, add up to 213 years against the scribe's total of 203. The last line is not part of the list but the signature of the scribe who wrote the prism, Nur-Ninshubur. Readings follow Langdon's 1923 edition, signs as his copy of the prism shows them; the names are read by sign (Shulgi for his Dungi, Amar-Suen for Bur-Sin, Ibi-Suen, Erra for his Gir*, Suen for Sin), with his forms in the notes. Where the copy differs from his print — signs he prints that are lost in a break, signs he restores that survive, a -ke₄ ('of', marking 'son of Ur-Ninurta' as the subject) that he does not print, no divine determinative before Lipit-Ashdar's name where he prints one, different signs in the names of the two kings he calls Bur-Sin — the copy is followed and the notes say so. His corrections of the figures (26 for 24, 5 kings for 4, 10 years for 20) are given in the notes; the prism's own figures are shown. Several of the Isin names are written with signs whose identification is uncertain, and they are flagged.

sentences.i: In Uruk, Utuhegal became king; he reigned 7⅙ (?) years and 7 days.
sentences.n: The fifth dynasty of Uruk: one king. VIII 3 'Unug-(ki)-ga ᵈUtu-ĝe-gál [lugal-ám]': UNUG, KI and GA, unug{ki}-ga 'in Uruk' (the locative -a written -ga after the g); then the divine determinative and UD, the sun-god Utu (Langdon's Utu here, not his usual Babbar), GAN (Langdon ĝe, read ḫe₂ by sign) and IG (ĝal₂) at the edge of a hatched break: Utuhegal, 'Utu is abundance'. lugal-am₃ 'was king' is lost and restored by Langdon (printed on a run-over line). VIII 4 'mu 7 šu-ši 7 ud [ni-ag]': MU, 7 diš (four over three), ŠU and IGI (šu-ši), 7 diš again, UD (u₄ 'day(s)') at the edge of the break; ni-ag 'he ruled' is lost and restored. The figure is the hard part. Elsewhere on this prism šu-ši is 'sixty', written as a word, with its multiplier before it (5 šu-ši = 300, II 30); read that way '7 šu-ši' would be 420. Langdon reads 'He reigned 7 1/6 years and 7 days', taking šu-ši alone as 1/6 of a year (two months) after the first 7 (fn. 7: 'šuš employed indifferently for 60 and 1/6', citing his Sumerian Grammar § 173). His reading is followed here, with a query: the signs show 'years 7, šu-ši, 7, days', and how they are to be grouped is not certain.

sentences.i: One king reigned 7⅙ (?) years and 7 days.
sentences.n: The total for the fifth dynasty of Uruk, over two lines. VIII 5 '1 lugal': a single upright (1) stands clear; the place of LUGAL, at the right of the line, is hatched on the copy, so lugal 'king' is shown as restored, though Langdon prints it unbracketed. VIII 6 'mu-bi 7 šu-ši 7 ud [ni- ag]': MU and BI, mu-bi 'its years', 7 diš, ŠU and IGI (šu-ši, read as in VIII 4: Langdon '7 1/6 years', queried), and 7 diš, whose lower wedges touch the edge of a break; then the copy is hatched, so u₄ 'days', which Langdon prints unbracketed, is shown as restored, with ni-ag 'he ruled' (Langdon restores the singular ni-ag here, not the ib-ag 'they ruled' of the other totals). The total repeats the one reign, as it should.

sentences.i: Uruk was smitten with weapons; its kingship was carried to Ur.
sentences.n: The refrain, over two lines. VIII 7 'Unug-(ki) ᵍⁱˢku ba- an sīg': UNUG and KI, GIŠ and KU ({ĝeš}tukul 'weapon(s)'), BA, AN and the compact sign read sig₃ (Langdon sīg): ba-an-sig₃ 'was smitten'; all clear, the signs spaced across the line. VIII 8 'nam-lugal-bi Uri[-(ki)-ma-šú ba-gín]': nam-lugal-bi 'its kingship', then ŠEŠ, the first element of urim₂ 'Ur', at the edge of a hatched break; the rest of the name and the ending are in the break and are Langdon's restoration, urim₂{ki}-ma-še₃ 'to Ur' (-še₃, his -šú, 'to'; the -ma- before it is written in his restoration and its function is not clear). At the right end of the line, beyond the break, the copy draws the DU sign, ĝen 'went', in the same form as at the end of VIII 22: Langdon brackets ba-gín whole, but ĝen survives, so only ba- is shown as restored.

sentences.i: In Ur, Ur-Namma became king; he reigned 18 years.
sentences.n: The third dynasty of Ur opens. VIII 9 'Uri-(ki)-ma Ur-ᵈNammu lugal': ŠEŠ, AB, KI and MA, urim₂{ki}-ma 'in Ur' (the locative -a written -ma after the final m); UR, clear; then the copy is hatched to the end of the line except for LUGAL, which stands clear at the right. The god's name, which Langdon prints unbracketed, is in the break here and is shown as restored; it is clear in VIII 11, written with the divine determinative and ENGUR (LAGAB×HAL), read namma (Langdon Nammu, after Gadd, fn. 8). No -am₃ follows lugal: literally 'Ur-Namma (was) king' (Langdon: 'At Ur Ur-Nammu was king'); the English follows the house formula 'In X, Y became king', as for the same construction in the pilot (Col. I 3, 'in-Eridu, Alulim (was) king') and in the Isin opening of VIII 23. VIII 10 'mu 18 ni- ag': MU; 18 = 1 u + 8 diš (four over four), the lower wedges at the edge of a break; NI is in the break (shown restored; Langdon prints it unbracketed) and AK clear at the right. Langdon (fn. 9) notes that here the Nippur text P. No. 5 Reverse begins.

sentences.i: Shulgi, son of Ur-Namma, reigned 46 years.
sentences.n: Two lines, all clear. VIII 11 'ᵈDungi dumu ᵈUr-ᵈNammu-ge': the divine determinative, then DUN and GI. Langdon reads the name Dungi; the first sign is DUN, read šul by sign (as in Šul-me-e, VII 32): {d}šul-gi, Shulgi. Both he and his father are written as gods, each with the divine determinative (Ur-Namma's not in VIII 9). dumu (TUR) 'son'; {d}ur-{d}namma, the god's name ENGUR (LAGAB×HAL) clear here; then KID, -ke₄ (Langdon -ge): genitive 'of' + the ergative, marking 'son of Ur-Namma' as the subject. VIII 12 'mu 46 ni- ag': 46 = 4 u + 6 diš (three over three). Langdon (fn. 1) holds 46 correct against the 58 of P. No. 3 Rev. 2, since 47 year-dates of this king were known to him, the last of them not counted by the scribes.

sentences.i: Amar-Suen, son of Shulgi, reigned 9 years.
sentences.n: Two lines, all clear. VIII 13 'ᵈBur-ᵈSin dumu ᵈDun-gi-ge': the divine determinative, then an open box with a diamond inside, AMAR 'calf', which Langdon reads bur; then the moon-god Suen (the divine determinative and EN.ZU; Langdon Sin): {d}amar-{d}suen, Amar-Suen, 'calf of Suen'. The Isin king of VIII 34 and 37, whom Langdon also calls Bur-Sin, is written on this copy with a different sign (see there). dumu; {d}šul-gi (here Langdon prints Dun-gi), and KID, -ke₄ 'of', marking the phrase as the subject. VIII 14 'mu 9 ni- ag': 9 diš (five over four).

sentences.i: Ibi-Suen, son of Shu-Suen, reigned 24 years.
sentences.n: Two lines, all clear. VIII 17 'I-be-ᵈSin dumu Gimil-ᵈSina-ge': I, then a sign drawn as a box with crossing wedges and a short tail, taken here as NE, read bi₂ (Langdon reads be, which would be the BAD sign, a single horizontal with a slanting wedge, not a box; the identification as NE is uncertain), then the moon-god Suen: i-bi₂-{d}suen, Ibi-Suen (Langdon 'Ibe-Sin'; 'Ibi-Sin' in his notes), an Akkadian name. dumu + šu-{d}suen (compact ŠU), then KID, -ke₄ 'of', marking the phrase as the subject. Langdon prints 'Gimil-ᵈSina-ge', with an a after Sin; the copy has no sign between ZU and KID, so no -a is shown. VIII 18 'mu 24 (26) ni-ag': the prism has 24 = 2 u + 4 diš (two over two). Langdon's '(26)' is his proposed correction, made to bring the dynasty's total nearer the 108 of VIII 20 (fn. 5); it is not on the prism. He notes (fn. 3) that P. No. 5 Rev. 5 has 25.

sentences.i: Four kings reigned 108 years.
sentences.n: The total for the third dynasty of Ur, over two lines, all clear. VIII 19 '5 (4) lugal': the prism has 4 diš (two over two) and LUGAL; Langdon prints '5 (4)' because five kings are named (Ur-Namma, Shulgi, Amar-Suen, Shu-Suen, Ibi-Suen) and notes 'Sic! The text has 4!' (fn. 4). The prism's 4 is shown and not corrected. VIII 20 'mu-bi 108 ib- ag': mu-bi; 108 = 1 geš (60) + 4 u + 8 diš (four over four); ib-ag 'they ruled'. The five reigns on the prism add up to 18 + 46 + 9 + 9 + 24 = 106, not 108. Langdon (fn. 5) gives the actual total as 106 and suggests reading 26 for Ibi-Suen (hence his '(26)' in VIII 18), or 47 for Shulgi and 25 for Ibi-Suen; he notes that the total on P. No. 5 is 117. Both the count and the total are reported as written, not corrected.

sentences.l: in-Ur (sic) with-weapons was-smitten; its-kingship to-Isin went.
sentences.i: Ur was smitten with weapons; its kingship was carried to Isin.
sentences.n: The refrain, over two lines, all clear. VIII 21 'Uri-(ki)-ma ᵍⁱˢku ba-an-sīg': ŠEŠ, AB, KI and MA, then {ĝeš}tukul 'weapon(s)' and ba-an-sig₃ 'was smitten' (Langdon sīg). The city is written with -ma, urim₂{ki}-ma, as in the opening formula 'in Ur' (VIII 9), where the refrain elsewhere has the bare name (Uruk in VIII 7); the literal line renders the -ma as written ('in-Ur (sic)', as 'to-X (sic)' for a misplaced -še₃ elsewhere), the English follows the formula. VIII 22 'nam-lugal-bi Ì-si-in-(ki)-šú ba-gín': nam-lugal-bi 'its kingship'; NI (read i₃; Langdon ì), SI, IN and KI, Isin, + EŠ₂, -še₃ 'to' (Langdon -šú); BA and DU, ba-ĝen 'went' (Langdon ba-gín).

sentences.i: In Isin, Ishbi-Erra became king; he reigned 33 years.
sentences.n: The dynasty of Isin opens; two lines, all clear. VIII 23 'Ì-si-in-(ki)-na Iš-bi-Gir*-ra lugal': NI, SI, IN, KI and NA, i₃-si-in{ki}-na 'in Isin' (the locative -a written -na after the final n). The king: IŠ, BI, then a sign drawn as a horizontal with slanting wedges and uprights, which Langdon marks with an asterisk as of uncertain reading (his Gir*), taken here as ARAD read er₃, then RA: iš-bi-er₃-ra, Ishbi-Erra (Langdon 'Ishbi-Girra'), the god's name Erra written here without the divine determinative (P. No. 5 Rev. 8 has it, Langdon fn. 6, who also cites a letter of Ibi-Suen about this man 'of Mari'). The identification of ARAD is uncertain. lugal, with no -am₃, as in VIII 9: literally '(was) king' (Langdon 'was king'), in English the formula 'became king'. VIII 24 'mu 33 ni-ag': 33 = 3 u + 3 diš. Langdon (fn. 7) notes that P. No. 5 Rev. 8 has 32, which must be raised to 33 to give that text's total.

sentences.n: Two lines, all clear. VIII 25 'ᵈGimil-ì-lí-šu dumu Iš-bi-Gir*-ra-ge': the divine determinative, ŠU (Langdon's Gimil, compact), NI, NI and ŠU: {d}šu-i₃-li₂-šu, Shu-ilishu, 'the one of his god' (Langdon fn. 8: P. No. 5 omits the determinative; so does this prism in VIII 27). dumu + iš-bi-er₃-ra (the same uncertain ARAD as in VIII 23) + KID, -ke₄ 'of', marking the phrase as the subject. VIII 26 'mu 20 (10) ni-ag': the prism has 20 = 2 u. Langdon's '(10)' is his preferred figure, from P. No. 5 Rev. 9, which he holds correct because only with 10 here do the Isin reigns add up to the 203 of VIII 45 (fn. 9); in his translation he sets them the other way round, '10 (20)'. The prism's 20 is shown and not corrected.

sentences.i: Idin-Dagan, son of Shu-ilishu, reigned 21 years.
sentences.n: Two lines. VIII 28 'mu 21 ni- ag': MU and 21 = 2 u + 1 diš are clear; the rest of the line is hatched on the copy, so ni-ag, which Langdon prints unbracketed, is shown as restored.

sentences.i: Ishme-Dagan, son of Idin-Dagan, reigned 20 years.
sentences.n: Two lines, the right half of each in a hatched break. sentences.l: Li[pit-Ashdar, son of Ishme-Dagan] — years [11 he-ruled].
sentences.i: Lipit-Ashdar, son of Ishme-Dagan, reigned 11 years.
sentences.n: Two lines, nearly all lost. VIII 31 'ᵈLi-[bi-it-Ašdar dumu Iš-me-ᵈDa-gan]': at the very start of the line LI (its corner-wedges and the closing upright, as in VIII 36) stands over a hatched patch, damaged but visible; the rest of the line is lost. No divine determinative is drawn: LI begins at the left edge of the column, where AN stands in VIII 36, so there is no room for it; Langdon prints ᵈ unbracketed, but the plate is followed and the name is shown without it (as Shu-ilishu is written without it in VIII 27). Langdon restores 'bi-it-Ašdar, son of Ishme-Dagan' from P. No. 5 Rev. 12 (fn. 11, noting that P. No. 2 X 7 has instead 'son of Idin-Dagan'). The restored BI and IT (the A₂ sign) are shown; his Ašdar, the goddess Ištar, is shown as a gap, since how it was written cannot be checked here (on this prism, in VI 17, his Ašdar is a single sign not identified). The name is Langdon's Lipit-Ashdar, Akkadian 'work of Ištar'; li-bi-it is written with BI, which he renders Lipit. VIII 32 'mu [11 ni- ag]': MU clear, the rest lost; 11 is restored from P. No. 2 X 8 and P. No. 5 Rev. 12 (fn. 12).

sentences.i: Ur-Ninurta reigned 28 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, mostly in a break. The divine determinative and UR are clear, then the copy is hatched to the end of the line, where AK (ag) stands clear. Langdon prints ᵈNinurta unbracketed, saying it is 'only partially preserved' (fn. 13), but nothing of it is drawn on the copy, so it is shown as restored, with mu 28 ni- 'years 28 he ruled'; he restores the name from P. No. 5 Rev. 14, where the god is written with IB, and notes that P. No. 2 X 9 preserves NIN; here the god is shown as NIN + IB (read urta). 28 = 2 u + 8 diš. Langdon (fn. 13) adds that on P. No. 2 X 10 this king's father was a man named after the god Adad, so that he was not descended from the kings before him: unlike his predecessors since Shu-ilishu, he is given no father here.

Ur-Ninurta (Langdon ᵈUr-ᵈNinurta) — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; ur 'man, servant' + the god Ninurta (NIN + IB, read urta): 'servant of Ninurta'; on this prism only {d}ur survives and the god's name is restored by Langdon from another copy

sentences.i: Bur-Suen, son of Ur-Ninurta, reigned 21 years.
sentences.n: Two lines. VIII 34 'ᵈBur-ᵈS[in dumu ᵈUr-ᵈNinurta]': the divine determinative; then a closed box with inner wedges, unlike the open box with a diamond (AMAR) of the Ur king Amar-Suen in VIII 13 and 15, whom Langdon also reads Bur-Sin; it is taken here as BUR, read bur, an identification from the drawing that is not certain (the same sign in VIII 37). Then the divine determinative and EN, damaged at the edge of a break (Langdon S[in): {d}bur-{d}suen, Bur-Suen. 'son of Ur-Ninurta' is in the break, restored by Langdon. Beyond the break, at the right end of the line, the copy draws a box of horizontals with upright heads, the KID of -ke₄ 'of' in VIII 13 and 17, which Langdon does not print: the line is read [dumu {d}ur-{d}nin-urta]-ke₄, 'son of Ur-Ninurta' marked as the subject, as in VIII 11, 13, 17, 25; the identification of the surviving sign is not certain. VIII 35 'mu 21 ni- ag': 21 = 2 u + 1 diš, the figure partly in a patch of hatching with a corner-wedge and an upright clear; Langdon's 21 is shown (unbracketed, since a wedge survives). NI and AK clear.

sentences.i: Lipit-Enlil, son of Bur-Suen, reigned 5 years.
sentences.n: Two lines; from here to VIII 43 the reign follows on the same line. VIII 36 'ᵈLi-bi-[it-ᵈ]En-lil': the divine determinative, LI (a cluster of corner-wedges), BI at the edge of a hatched patch; IT and the god's determinative are in the break, restored by Langdon; EN and KID (lil₂) clear at the right: {d}li-bi-it-{d}en-lil₂, Lipit-Enlil (Langdon's English), 'work of Enlil'. Langdon (fn. 1) restores P. No. 5 Rev. 15 with this name as the eighth king and says he is otherwise unknown in documents of the period. VIII 37 'dumu Bur-ᵈSin-ge mu 5 ni-ag': dumu, then the closed-box sign taken as BUR (as in VIII 34) with no divine determinative before it, the moon-god Suen, and KID, -ke₄ 'of'; mu, 5 diš (three over two), ni-ag; all clear.

sentences.i: Erra-imiti reigned 8 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, all clear. The divine determinative; the sign Langdon reads Gir* (as in Ishbi-Erra, VIII 23), taken as ARAD read er₃, and RA: the god Erra; then I, MI, TI: {d}er₃-ra-i-mi-ti, Erra-imiti (Langdon 'Girra-imiti'), an Akkadian name whose second part is not clear. 8 diš (four over four). Langdon (fn. 2) notes that P. No. 5 Rev. 16 has 7 years and that King's Chronicles write the name ᵈGir*-ra-ZAG-LU; in his note to VIII 45 he argues that the scribe of this prism, who leaves out a reign of six months after this king, has added it to this one, giving 8 for 7.

sentences.i: Enlil-bani reigned 24 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, all clear. The divine determinative, EN and KID (lil₂), BA, NI: {d}en-lil₂-ba-ni, Enlil-bani (Langdon 'Enlilbani'), Akkadian 'Enlil is creator'. 24 = 2 u + 4 diš (two over two). Langdon (fn. 3) notes that P. No. 5 Rev. 17 has here six months for a king whose name is obliterated and who is omitted on this prism, and Rev. 18 [ᵈEn-lil-ba]-ni with 24 years.

sentences.i: Zambiya reigned 3 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, all clear. The divine determinative, ZA, AM, BI and IA (Langdon i̯a, the sound ya): {d}za-am-bi-ia, Zambiya (Langdon 'Zambija'); the sense of the name is not clear. 3 diš.

sentences.i: Iterpisha reigned 4 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, all clear. The divine determinative; I; a sign with corner-wedges, uprights and a long horizontal, taken as DI, read ṭe after Langdon (not the box-with-diagonals TE of I-ba-te, VII 37); IR, read er (Langdon ir; the sign has both values); a large box with horizontals, taken as KA and read pi₄ (Langdon pî; Akkadian pû 'mouth'); ŠA. Langdon (fn. 4) reads the name ᵈI-ṭe-ir-pî-ša, 'Iterpîsha', from eṭir-pî-ša 'her word saves', confirmed for him by a date 'year Iterpiša (became) king' in Legrain, PBS 13 No. 4; Hilprecht cites tablets of ᵈI-te-ir-KA-ša. The identifications of DI and KA are uncertain; and on the copy the stretch between the divine determinative and MU is drawn in four groups of wedges that do not part cleanly into five signs, so the sign-by-sign assignment here follows Langdon's reading rather than the drawing. 4 diš (two over two).

Iterpisha (Langdon ᵈI-ṭe-ir-pî-ša, 'Iterpîsha') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; I + DI (ṭe) + IR (er) + KA (read pi₄, Akkadian pû 'mouth') + ŠA; Langdon derives it from eṭir-pî-ša 'her word saves' and notes another writing with KA (Hilprecht's I-te-ir-KA-ša); the identifications of the second and fourth signs are uncertain

sentences.i: Ur-dukuga reigned 4 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, all clear. The divine determinative, UR, then a box with a diagonal and horizontals, taken after Langdon's dù as KAK (du₃) — the drawing does not settle it; then KU₃ 'pure, holy' and GA: {d}ur-du₃-ku₃-ga, Ur-dukuga (Langdon 'Ur-dukugga'; his print sets a mark over the g of -ga, a printing flaw). Langdon (fn. 5) cites a date of this king, 'year when Ur-dukugga dug the canal Imgur-Ninsubur' (Chiera, PBS VIII No. 10), and the name Ur-du-kug-ga in a document of Enlil-bani's reign. 4 diš.

Ur-dukuga (Langdon ᵈUr-dù-kug-ga, 'Ur-dukugga') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; ur 'man, servant' + a sign Langdon reads dù (taken as KAK, read du₃) + KU₃ 'pure, holy' + GA; the second sign is not certainly identified on the copy and the sense of the name is not clear

sentences.i: Suen-magir reigned 11 years.
sentences.n: Name and reign on one line, all clear; the last reign on the prism. The divine determinative, EN.ZU, the moon-god Suen (Langdon Sin), MA, and a box with corner-wedges taken as GIR₂ (Langdon gir; the identification is uncertain): {d}suen-ma-gir₂, Suen-magir (Langdon 'Sin-magir'), Akkadian 'Suen is favourable'. 11 = 1 u + 1 diš. Langdon (fn. 6 to VIII 45) holds that the prism was written at the end of this king's reign, since the last king of the dynasty in other lists is not given.

morph.gloss: divine determinative (diĝir) — marks the following name as a god

Suen-magir (Langdon ᵈSin-ma-gir, 'Sin-magir') — king of Isin, the last named on this prism, in whose reign Langdon thinks it was written; the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, with the divine determinative) + MA + a sign taken as GIR₂ (read gir₂; Langdon gir): Akkadian 'Suen is favourable'; the identification of the last sign is uncertain
year(s) · name — in lugal-mu nu-tuk, taken with Langdon as 'had no king by name'; the sense there is uncertain
ì-aĝ₂ (Langdon 'ni-ag') — 'he ruled', lit. 'measured out'; reign verb, 3sg

sentences.i: Fourteen kings reigned 203 years.
sentences.n: The total for the dynasty of Isin, over two lines, all clear; a double ruled line follows. VIII 44 '14 lugal': 14 = 1 u + 4 diš, and LUGAL; fourteen kings are named (VIII 23–43). VIII 45 'mu-bi 203 ib-ag': mu-bi; 203 = 3 geš (180) + 2 u + 3 diš; ib-ag 'they ruled'. The fourteen reigns on the prism add up to 33 + 20 + 21 + 20 + 11 + 28 + 21 + 5 + 8 + 24 + 3 + 4 + 4 + 11 = 213, of which 20 and 11 (VIII 30, 32) and 28 (VIII 33) are restored. Langdon (fn. 6) gives the actual total as 213, 'but see line 26': with 10 for Shu-ilishu, as in P. No. 5, the sum is 203. He adds that the prism was written at the end of Suen-magir's reign, the last king being omitted, and that its scribe leaves out a reign of six months after Erra-imiti, which P. No. 5 counts: with that king the list would have 15 kings and 226 years against 225½ on P. No. 5, so the scribe must have added the six months to Erra-imiti (8 years for 7). The total is shown as written, not corrected.

morph.gloss: fourteen
king (here plural 'kings')
'its years' — mu 'years' + -bi 'its'
60 (the base of the system); 3 here = 180
1; 3 here = 3
íb-aĝ₂ — 'they ruled' (plural reign verb)

sentences.i: By the hand of Nur-Ninshubur.
sentences.n: Not a line of the King List but the scribe's signature (a colophon), written below the double ruled line that closes the list. ŠU 'hand', which Langdon reads with the Akkadian word, kat (qāt 'hand of'), read šu here by sign; then NU, UR₂ (Langdon ùr), the divine determinative, NIN and ŠUBUR (Langdon subur): nu-ur₂-{d}nin-šubur, Nur-Ninshubur (Langdon 'Nur-Ninsubur'), Akkadian 'light of Ninshubur'. 'By the hand of' is the usual way a scribe signs his tablet: Nur-Ninshubur wrote this prism. Langdon leaves the line unnumbered in his transliteration and numbers it 46 in his translation; all its signs are clear.

morph.gloss: hand — the ŠU sign; in a scribe's colophon šu X 'by the hand of X', i.e. 'written by X' (Langdon reads it with the Akkadian word, kat, for qāt 'hand of')
divine determinative (diĝir) — marks the following name as a god

Nur-Ninshubur (Langdon Nu-ùr-ᵈNin-subur, 'Nur-Ninsubur') — the scribe who wrote this prism, named in its colophon; NU + UR₂ (Langdon ùr) + the goddess Ninshubur (NIN + ŠUBUR, with the divine determinative): Akkadian nūr 'light (of)', 'light of Ninshubur'
